sentences: Before we start, I've got a quick story of my own.
I tried to make a new recipe last night.
I followed the instructions but forgot to add the eggs until the end, so I had to mix everything again.
Have you had a go at making anything recently?

Yeah, I went to my nan's on Sunday and we made biscuits, like the ones with the icing on top, except hers weren't the normal sort because she uses this recipe from a book she got ages ago, and it's got a different ratio of butter to flour.
If you change the ratio, the texture changes, which is why some biscuits are crunchy and some are more crumbly.
You and your nan made biscuits on Sunday.
What happened while you were making them?

Well, the recipe says chill the dough for thirty minutes, but we didn't have enough room in the fridge because there was a casserole dish on the shelf, and then Nan said we could put it in the freezer for ten minutes instead, which isn't exactly the same thing because the temperature is lower and you have to be careful not to freeze it solid.
What did you do with the dough?
I put it in the freezer and set the timer on my phone for ten minutes.
It was on 14:22, so when it went off it was 14:32.
What happened when the timer went off?
It was a bit harder round the edges.
Butter has a melting point of about thirty-two to thirty-five degrees Celsius, which is why it softens quite quickly in your hands.
And what did you do next?
We used the star cutter and the round cutter.
The star one has five points, obviously, and the round one was about six centimetres across.
Did the biscuits go straight into the oven?
No, we put them on the baking tray first.
There were twelve stars and eight circles, so twenty altogether.
Nan said there wasn't enough space for another one.
What was it like making them with your nan?
She let me do the measuring without checking every five seconds.
It sounds like you really enjoyed having that independence.
Well, I know how to measure flour.
It's not difficult if you use the scales properly.
We iced them after they'd cooled down.
So you made the dough with your nan, chilled it in the freezer for ten minutes, cut out twenty biscuits and iced them when they were cool.
You liked that Nan let you do the measuring yourself.
Yeah, and next time we're making shortbread, which is different because it doesn't normally have egg in it and the proportions are different.
We can hear about the shortbread next time.
